reason: The cited evidence (E1–E4) directly demonstrates N-doping of a PtCoFeNiCu HEA via ammonia treatment, formation of a Pt-rich shell and multiple M–N bonds, and resulting durability improvements, but the evidence is from electrocatalytic ORR conditions, not automotive exhaust with H2O and NO, so the transfer to the proposed exhaust environment is a gap.
premises: Ammonia annealing at ~600–650°C can incorporate nitrogen into a multi-element alloy to form multiple metal–nitrogen bonds
Nitrogen doping creates a Pt-rich protective surface layer on the alloy
Metal–nitrogen bonds (especially Ni–N, Co–N) suppress dissolution and sintering of transition metals
The Pt-rich shell and lattice distortion from N-doping enhance durability under corrosive conditions
The treatment maintains low PGM consumption while improving activity retention
